(November 23, 2026) – Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced positive 16-week results from the BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial of KT-621, its first-in-class, once-daily oral STAT6 degrader, in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The trial met its primary endpoint of percent change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 16 and secondary endpoints, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo across all dose cohorts. The BROADEN2 findings support advancement of KT-621 into late-stage development, with the first Phase 3 AD trial planned to initiate by mid-2027, subject to alignment with regulators, as well as potential expansion in other Type 2 indications. “Today’s results mark a pivotal moment in the field of immunology, demonstrating what truly groundbreaking science can achieve in areas of significant patient need. The BROADEN2 results exceeded our expectations, reinforcing our belief that KT-621 represents one of the largest opportunities in biopharma, with the potential to transform care for millions of people living with Type 2 inflammatory diseases,” said Nello Mainolfi, PhD, Founder, President and CEO, Kymera Therapeutics. “What stands out is the combination of improvements in disease severity and itch beginning as early as Week 1, significant continued responses across all dose cohorts at Week 16, and a favorable safety profile. The overall clinical activity supports the potential to deliver the level of disease control historically reported with approved biologics such as dupilumab. The mid dose, which we selected to achieve optimal STAT6 pharmacology, consistently delivered the largest numerical improvements across endpoints and is well positioned to advance towards Phase 3.” Dr. Mainolfi continued, “These findings strengthen our conviction that KT-621 could substantially expand the number of patients receiving an advanced therapy. By overcoming the longstanding scientific challenge of directly targeting STAT6, we have taken a clear step toward our vision of delivering the first oral therapy for the full spectrum of Type 2 diseases, beginning in AD. Additionally, these results validate the scientific expertise and translational capabilities behind our innovation engine and our approach of pairing the right targets with the right technology to create a new era of oral medicines. As we advance KT-621 toward Phase 3, we are building an expanding franchise with the potential to reshape care across immunology. Importantly, we thank the patients and their families for their trust and commitment, and the investigators and study teams for their dedication to advancing this unique new treatment for AD.” “In my practice, I see many patients living with AD who continue to struggle with persistent symptoms and the daily burden of managing this chronic condition,” said Eric Simpson, MD, MCR, lead investigator on the BROADEN2 study and Frances J. Storrs Medical Dermatology Professor and Director of CLEAR Eczema Center, Oregon Health & Science University. “A targeted oral therapy that combines robust clinical activity with favorable safety and tolerability could expand the number of patients receiving systemic treatment and help them achieve and maintain disease control. KT-621 brings an innovative mechanism to a well-established pathway in Type 2 inflammation by targeting STAT6. The highly encouraging BROADEN2 findings suggest a compelling profile and reinforce the potential of this program to address the substantial unmet need in AD.” BROADEN2 Phase 2b Trial Design and Baseline Characteristics BROADEN2 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging trial evaluating the clinical activity, safety and tolerability of KT-621 in 244 adult and adolescent patients with moderate to severe AD. Patients were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive a low dose (n=61), mid dose (n=61) or high dose (n=63) of KT-621, or placebo (n=59), once daily for 16 weeks. Patients completing 16 weeks of treatment were eligible to participate in a 52-week open-label extension following the treatment period. Baseline characteristics were generally balanced across the four treatment groups. The mean baseline EASI score was approximately 28, and the mean baseline Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS) score was 7.1. Patients with severe disease based on a validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) score of 4 represented 38% of the study population, and 33% of patients had received prior biologic therapy. Of the 244 randomized patients, 234 completed the 16-week double-blind treatment period, and 230 of those patients enrolled in the open-label extension. About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited. About Deramiocel Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe.
